claim: On 19 May 2020 (effective 15 May 2020) BIS published an interim final rule at 85 FR 29849 amending General Prohibition Three, the foreign-produced direct product rule, to control certain foreign-produced items destined to Entity List entities with a 'footnote 1' designation, and applied it to Huawei and its listed affiliates.

A foreign-produced item is subject to the new control if the entity for which the item is destined has a footnote 1 designation in the Entity List. This rule also applies this new control to Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. (Huawei) and its non-U.S. affiliates listed as entities."

claim: The May 2020 Huawei FDP rule reached foreign-made items that were the direct product of technology or software produced or developed by Huawei, or produced by a non-US plant that is itself a direct product of US-origin technology or software.

claim: Under the May 2020 Huawei FDP rule, foreign-produced items that had started production before 15 May 2020 were exempt if exported, reexported or transferred before 14 September 2020.

evidence: "In supplement no. 3 to part 732 (BIS's 'Know Your Customer' Guidance and Red Flags), this IFR adds eight new Red Flags under paragraphs (b)(20) through (27)" (89 FR 96790, preamble)

claim: Under 15 CFR 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(B), foreign-produced SME that is subject to the EAR only through the SME de minimis rule or the SME FDP rule is excluded from the licence requirement when exported from abroad by an entity located in a Supplement No. 4 country that is not headquartered, and whose ultimate parent is not headquartered, in Macau or a Country Group D:5 destination.
evidence: "An item subject to the EAR pursuant to § 734.4(a)(8) or § 734.9(k) if the item is reexported or exported from abroad by an entity located in a country specified in supplement no. 4 to this part, and the entity is not headquartered or have an ultimate parent company headquartered in either Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5." (15 CFR 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(B), eCFR 2026-09-01)

claim: Inference: because South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Israel are not in Supplement No. 4 to Part 742, SME made there that falls under the SME FDP or SME de minimis rule needs a US licence for China, whereas the same tools made by Japanese or Dutch firms do not (they fall under national Japanese/Dutch controls instead).
evidence: Our reading of the exclusion in 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(B) together with the Supplement No. 4 country list.
notes: Based on this batch's claims on 15 CFR 742.4(a)(4)(ii)(B) and the Supplement No. 4 country list; whether specific Korean/Taiwanese tools meet the FDP product scope was not checked.

claim: Under the EAR's general de minimis rules (15 CFR 734.4), foreign-made items with controlled US content above 10% of value are subject to the EAR when reexported to Country Group E:1/E:2 destinations, and above 25% for other destinations.
evidence: paraphrase: 15 CFR 734.4(c) (10% level, applies worldwide incl. E:1/E:2) and 734.4(d) (25% level, for countries other than Country Groups E:1 or E:2); e.g. "Reexports of a foreign-made commodity incorporating controlled U.S.-origin commodities...valued at 10% or less of the total value" (eCFR 2026-09-01)

claim: There is no de minimis level under the SME FDP rule for foreign tools meeting ECCN 3B001.a.4, c, d, f.1, f.5, f.6, k to n, p.2, p.4, r or 3B002.c: any US-origin IC content makes them subject to the EAR for Macau and Country Group D:5.
evidence: "There is no de minimis level related to the SME FDP rule for a commodity meeting the parameters in ECCNs 3B001.a.4, c, d, f.1, f.5, f.6, k to n, p.2, p.4, r, or 3B002.c" (15 CFR 734.4(a)(8), eCFR 2026-09-01)

claim: As of September 2026, 15 CFR 734.9 contains FDP rules for national security items, 9x515, 600 series, Entity List footnotes 1, 4 and 5, Russia/Belarus/Crimea, Russia/Belarus military end users, advanced computing, supercomputers, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and AI model weights.

claim: The advanced computing FDP rule (734.9(h)) can reach foreign-produced items destined to any location worldwide when its product and destination scope conditions are met, while the SME FDP rule (734.9(k)) applies when there is knowledge the item is destined to Macau or a Country Group D:5 destination.
evidence: (h)(2): "A foreign-produced item meets the destination scope of this paragraph (h)(2) if there is 'knowledge' that the foreign-produced item is: (i) Destined to any location worldwide..."; (k): "...if there is 'knowledge' that the foreign-produced item is destined to Macau or a destination in Country Group D:5..." evidence: paraphrase: Miller & Chevalier (12 Aug 2026): the rule was informally rescinded on May 13, 2025 but remains in the CFR; BIS said "the informal rescission left the pre-existing regulations in place" with non-enforcement in the interim (tool summary)

claim: No BIS rule rescinding the AI Diffusion Rule appears in the Federal Register list of BIS rules published between 17 January 2025 and 30 September 2026.

Absence in this listing does not rule out another instrument.

claim: Interpretation: the US semiconductor export-control regime works through five stacked layers: (1) item controls by ECCN and threshold (3A090, 4A090, 3B001/3B090/3B993, 3D/3E); (2) end-use controls on advanced fabs and supercomputers (744.23); (3) end-user controls via the Entity List and VEU; (4) extraterritorial reach via FDP and de minimis rules; and (5) controls on US persons' activities (744.6).
evidence: Synthesis of this batch's claims on 87 FR 62186, 88 FR 73424/73458, 89 FR 96790, 15 CFR 734.4, 734.9, 742.4 and 744.6.
notes: Built from this batch's claims on ECCN 3A090/4A090/3B090, 744.23 thresholds, 744.6(c)(2), 734.9 FDP list, 734.4(a)(8) and the VEU revocation.

claim: Interpretation: the regime evolved from company-specific measures (Huawei 2019-20, SMIC 2020) to country-wide technology thresholds for China (October 2022), then to anti-circumvention refinements (October 2023 performance density, 40+ countries), then to FDP rules reaching foreign tools and HBM (December 2024) and supply-chain due diligence on foundries and OSATs (January 2025); 2025-26 changes mostly adjusted licensing and end-user lists rather than adding new item controls.
evidence: Our reading of the dated rule sequence recorded in this batch.
notes: Built from this batch's dated rule claims (84 FR 22961, 85 FR 51596, 85 FR 83416, 87 FR 62186, 88 FR 73424/73458, 89 FR 96790, 90 FR 5298, 90 FR 42321, 2026 rule list) and existing CLM-0305 to CLM-0309.
